Notes:

1. Role line. I used "Self-represented" because that is the wording in your draft. If the case caption designates the party (Plaintiff, Defendant, Petitioner, Respondent), use that, for example "Plaintiff, pro se".

2. Placeholders. The draft gave no date, address, telephone number or email address. A Wisconsin paper signed by an unrepresented party should state these (Wis. Stat. § 802.05(1)). I left clearly marked placeholders and did not invent any. I also did not add a state bar number, since there is none to supply for a self-represented party.

3. Signature line. For eFiling, Wis. Stat. § 801.18(12) permits either "Electronically signed by [NAME]" or a handwritten signature applied before imaging. A paper filing by a party needs an actual handwritten signature, and a typed "/s/" alone is not a substitute. The line is formatting only, not an executed signature. Alex Example must adopt and sign it personally. I have not signed for anyone. The "Signature status: unsigned draft" line should come out once it is signed, or before it is filed.

4. Styling. By default the "Electronically signed by Alex Example" line is in italics and the lines below it are in plain type. Italics are a style preference, not a legal requirement. The block sits on the right half of the page, indented about 3 inches. Plain text cannot show that, so apply it in your word processor.

5. Not checked. I did not review the substance, the court, the caption, the case number, the deadlines or the service method, and I did not check whether any local rule applies. Nothing here has been verified against current rules, and the draft is not ready to file on this review alone.
